question: Q10
answer:
# CURE-CHECK SEQUENCE — ADHESIVE COUPON IN A GUARDED LABORATORY OVEN
Doc ID: CC-ADH-001 Rev 1 | Scope: one adhesive coupon, coupon probe already installed | Logging interval: 1 s | Units: C, s

## 1. Scope and standing assumptions
1.1 The coupon-mounted temperature probe is the sole authority for band compliance. Oven setpoint (120 C) and oven-air temperature are recorded for context only and are never the acceptance variable.
1.2 In-band means 118.0 C <= T <= 122.0 C, both endpoints inclusive.
1.3 The hold window is the closed interval [t0, t0 + 600 s], where t0 is the timestamp of the first logged coupon-probe sample that is in-band. Warm-up before t0 is uncontrolled and lies outside the window.
1.4 An excursion is any single sample inside the window with T < 118.0 C or T > 122.0 C. No averaging, no smoothing, no grace period, no retrospective re-reading of the data.
1.5 Assess the run means: evaluate the frozen window against acceptance criteria AC-1 to AC-6 and record PASS or FAIL per criterion plus an overall result. It is a time-in-band compliance check, not a destructive cure-state test (no lap-shear, DSC or coupon destruction is part of this sequence).
1.6 Guarded means the oven guard/door is interlocked and stays closed and latched from the start of heating until the coupon probe reads <= 40 C at S12.
1.7 Cooling is passive, inside the de-energized oven, guard closed.
1.8 No restart: a failed or aborted run is closed as FAILED or NO HOLD. The same coupon may not be re-run, and the same run ID may not be reused. A further attempt requires a new coupon, a new run ID and re-authorization under the work instruction.

## 2. Equipment and record setup (placeholders to be filled at execution)
Run ID, coupon ID, oven ID, probe ID, probe calibration due date, operator, date/time (single clock, ISO 8601), ambient temperature, setpoint applied, sample interval.

## 3. Pre-checks (complete before any heating)
P1 Record probe ID and confirm calibration is within its due date; record the stated measurement uncertainty. An out-of-calibration probe means the run cannot be assessed — stop before heating.
P2 Prove the guard interlock functional per the oven SOP (door open => heating inhibited).
P3 Set the independent over-temperature cut-out to 130 C. It must be above the 122.0 C band ceiling so it can never truncate a conforming hold, and below the oven rating. Never raise it to rescue a run.
P4 Arm the logger: 1 s interval, coupon-probe channel plus oven-air channel, all timestamps from one clock.
P5 PPE: heat-resistant gloves for any handling; the <= 40 C rule exists so removal is safe, not so gloves can be skipped.
P6 Confirm the coupon is seated and the probe attached per the work instruction, and the guard is closed and latched.

## 4. Sequence
S1 — Record the header: run ID, coupon ID, oven ID, probe ID, calibration due, operator, date/time, ambient temperature, intended setpoint 120 C.
S2 — Set the oven setpoint to 120 C and energize heating. Confirm the guard is closed and latched. Do not open the guard again until S12.
S3 — Start logging at 1 s and confirm both channels are recording. t0 is not yet defined.
S4 — Wait for entry: watch for the first sample with 118.0 <= T <= 122.0. Record that timestamp as t0 and record T(t0). Do not adjust the setpoint. Note: the coupon lags oven air, so oven air may pass 122 C before the coupon does — that is not an excursion because it is outside the window.
S5 — Start the 600 s hold timer at t0; the window is [t0, t0 + 600 s].
S6 — During the hold: no guard opening, no setpoint change, no probe manipulation, no coupon handling. Any guard opening or setpoint change during the window voids the run and is recorded as a failure event.
S7 — Excursion test, evaluated on every sample of the window. The first out-of-band sample is an excursion event: record its time t_e and temperature T_e, mark the run FAILED, stop the hold, go to S10 and then to section 7.
S8 — At t0 + 600 s, freeze the window and record: hold duration, sample count, minimum temperature with its time, maximum temperature with its time, excursion count with event list, and the largest logging gap.
S9 — Assess: apply AC-1 to AC-6 to the frozen window; record PASS or FAIL for each and the overall result.
S10 — Switch off heating (setpoint to off/0, heaters de-energized). Leave the guard closed and the coupon in place.
S11 — Cooldown in place: log the coupon probe at 60 s intervals (or leave the 1 s log running). Do not open the guard and do not touch the coupon until the probe reads <= 40 C.
S12 — Removal and closeout: when the probe reads <= 40 C, record the cooldown-complete time and temperature, open the guard, remove the coupon, record the removal time, sign and date, and attach the verdict.

## 5. Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | Limit | Basis |
|----|-----------|-------|-------|
| AC-1 | Setpoint applied and recorded | exactly 120 C | Setup verification only; not the acceptance variable |
| AC-2 | Hold duration | 600.0 s, continuous | Timer started at t0 |
| AC-3 | Minimum coupon-probe temperature in window | >= 118.0 C | Lower band edge, inclusive |
| AC-4 | Maximum coupon-probe temperature in window | <= 122.0 C | Upper band edge, inclusive |
| AC-5 | Excursion count in window | 0 | Any single out-of-band sample fails the run |
| AC-6 | Logging continuity in window | no gap > 2 s | At 1 s nominal sampling; continuity must be provable |
| AC-7 | Removal temperature (closeout gate) | <= 40 C | Must be recorded before removal; does not alter the hold verdict |
Run verdict = PASS only if AC-1 through AC-6 all pass. AC-7 gates removal and closeout of the record.

## 6. Completed log — this run
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Run ID | CC-ADH-001-R01 |
| Coupon ID | ADH-COUPON-01 |
| Oven ID | OV-LAB-01 |
| Probe ID | TC-COUPON-01 (calibration due date recorded at S1) |
| Operator / date | recorded at S1 |
| Setpoint | 120 C |
| Sample interval | 1 s |
| t0 (first in-band sample) | recorded at S4 |
| Hold window | t0 to t0 + 600 s |
| Hold duration | 600 s (uninterrupted) |
| Samples in window | 601 |
| Minimum temperature | 119 C (time recorded) |
| Maximum temperature | 121 C (time recorded) |
| Excursions | 0 |
| Largest logging gap | none (<= 2 s) |
| Assessment AC-1 to AC-6 | PASS / PASS / PASS / PASS / PASS / PASS |
| Heating switched off | recorded at S10 |
| Cooldown complete | recorded at S12, probe <= 40 C |
| Removal | recorded at S12 |
| Verdict | PASS |

## 7. Assessment of this run and verdict
7.1 AC-2: recorded duration 600 s against a 600 s timer — PASS.
7.2 AC-3: minimum 119 C against a lower limit of 118.0 C — PASS, margin 1.0 C.
7.3 AC-4: maximum 121 C against an upper limit of 122.0 C — PASS, margin 1.0 C.
7.4 AC-5: zero excursions — PASS. AC-6: no logging gap above 2 s — PASS.
7.5 VERDICT: PASS. Run CC-ADH-001-R01 is an uninterrupted 600 s hold with the coupon probe inside the inclusive 118–122 C band throughout (minimum 119 C, maximum 121 C, zero excursions).
7.6 AC-7 remains open until the S12 cooldown record is entered; it gates removal and record closeout and does not change the hold verdict.

## 8. Failure and abort handling (no restart)
8.1 Excursion: record t_e and T_e, stop the hold, switch off heating (S10), cool in place to <= 40 C, remove the coupon, mark the coupon NON-CONFORMING and quarantine it, close the run as FAILED.
8.2 Abort before t0 (coupon never enters the band, oven fault, probe failure, guard opened during warm-up): switch off heating, cool to <= 40 C, close the run as NO HOLD. This is not a PASS and not a restart.
8.3 No restart is permitted: the failed coupon is not re-run and the run ID is not reused. A new attempt needs a new coupon, a new run ID and re-authorization.

## 9. Edge cases and notes
9.1 Exactly 118.0 C is in-band; exactly 122.0 C is in-band. 117.9 C and 122.1 C are excursions.
9.2 Oven-air readings outside the band are never excursions; only the coupon probe counts.
9.3 Probe dropout, open circuit or an implausible reading means continuity cannot be proven: treat as a run failure, not a data gap to be interpolated.
9.4 Duration is computed from timestamps, not from the sample count.
9.5 Detection resolution equals the sample interval (1 s). The compliance claim is therefore per-sample at 1 s, and that is stated on the record.
9.6 A fast warm-up can carry the coupon through the band quickly; if the sample after t0 is already above 122.0 C the run fails at that sample under AC-5 — there is no catch-up provision.

## 10. Safety
10.1 Oven and coupon surfaces are at 120 C during the hold. Keep the guard latched; opening it is both a burn hazard and an automatic run failure.
10.2 Heat-resistant gloves for any handling; removal only at a recorded probe temperature <= 40 C.
10.3 The independent over-temperature cut-out stays at 130 C; do not defeat or raise it during a run.
10.4 On any abnormal smell, smoke or uncontrolled heating: de-energize the oven at the local isolator, do not open the guard until the probe reads <= 40 C, and record the event against the run.

items.detail: the oven is set to 120 deg C, the coupon probe must enter the 118-122 deg C band, and only then does the timer start
the 600 s hold inside the inclusive band, with any excursion failing without restart, is stated
the logged 119-121 deg C range throughout the 600 s hold satisfies every criterion: PASS
heating is switched off, the coupon cools inside to at most 40 deg C at the coupon probe, and only then is it removed

question: Q11
answer:
Let the 20-tooth gear be the driver and the 60-tooth gear be the driven gear. Take clockwise rotation as positive when viewed from the chosen side of both parallel shafts.

Speed:
  n_out = n_in × (N_driver / N_driven)
        = 900 rpm × (20 / 60)
        = 300 rpm

Because the mesh is external, the driven gear rotates opposite to the driver. Therefore the output speed is 300 rpm in the counterclockwise direction when the input is clockwise, viewed from the same side of both parallel shafts.

Torque:
For an ideal lossless gear pair, power is conserved:
  P_in = P_out
  T_in ω_in = T_out ω_out
  T_out = T_in × (ω_in / ω_out)
        = T_in × (N_driven / N_driver)
        = 3.00 N·m × (60 / 20)
        = 9.00 N·m

The transmitted torque magnitude on the output shaft is therefore 9.00 N·m. The torque delivered to a driven load acts in the same sense as the output rotation (counterclockwise for the stated input direction); only its magnitude is requested here.

Final answers:
- Output speed: 300 rpm
- Rotation direction: counterclockwise, opposite the clockwise input, viewed from the same side of both parallel shafts
- Transmitted torque magnitude: 9.00 N·m

question: Q12
answer:
ANSWER — 40 CFR §141.62(b), July 1, 2014 edition, for a community drinking-water system

Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) in mg/L:

| Contaminant | §141.62(b) paragraph | MCL | Applicability in §141.62(b) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Arsenic | (b)(16) | 0.010 mg/L | Community water systems and non-transient non-community water systems |
| Fluoride | (b)(1) | 4.0 mg/L | Community water systems only |
| Nitrate | (b)(7) | 10 mg/L as Nitrogen | Community water systems; non-transient non-community water systems; transient non-community water systems |

Thus, for a community water system, the §141.62(b) MCLs are:
- Arsenic: 0.010 mg/L
- Fluoride: 4.0 mg/L
- Nitrate: 10 mg/L as N

Chemical reporting basis for nitrate:
The table entry is “(7) Nitrate 10 (as Nitrogen).” The specified basis is therefore **as nitrogen (as N)**, i.e., the MCL is expressed as mg/L of nitrogen in nitrate (NO3-N), not as mg/L of the nitrate ion (NO3). The regulation's nitrate MCL is 10 mg/L as N. For context only, that is equivalent to about 44.3 mg/L as NO3 using the ratio 62.004/14.007 ≈ 4.427; the regulatory reporting basis remains “as Nitrogen,” and 44.3 mg/L as NO3 is not the §141.62(b) MCL as printed.

Distinctions to avoid error:
- Nitrate is §141.62(b)(7): 10 mg/L as N. Nitrite is §141.62(b)(8): 1 mg/L as N. Total nitrate and nitrite is §141.62(b)(9): 10 mg/L as N. These are separate entries.
- Fluoride's §141.62(b)(1) MCL is 4.0 mg/L. The 2.0 mg/L fluoride secondary standard is not the §141.62(b) MCL and is not the value requested.
- Arsenic's MCL in the July 1, 2014 edition is 0.010 mg/L; the arsenic MCL was effective January 23, 2006 under §141.60(b)(4), so it is present in the 2014 edition.

Source basis: 40 CFR §141.62(b), July 1, 2014 edition (CFR-2014-title40-vol23, §141.62), table entries (b)(1), (b)(7), and (b)(16); effective-date confirmation at §141.60(b).

question: Q13
answer:
Series RC charging calculation

Given:
- Ideal DC source: V0 = 10.0 V, connected at t = 0
- Resistor: R = 10.0 kΩ = 1.00×10^4 Ω
- Capacitor: C = 100 µF = 1.00×10^-4 F, initially uncharged, Vc(0) = 0
- Observation time: t = 2.00 s

Sign convention for current:
Positive current is defined as flowing from the source toward the capacitor. With this convention, the capacitor voltage increases when i is positive, and the charging current is positive.

1. Time constant
τ = RC = (1.00×10^4 Ω)(1.00×10^-4 F) = 1.00 s

2. Capacitor voltage at t = 2.00 s
For an initially uncharged capacitor in a series RC circuit:
Vc(t) = V0(1 - e^(-t/τ))

At t = 2.00 s:
t/τ = 2.00 s / 1.00 s = 2.00
e^(-2.00) = 0.135335283

Vc(2.00 s) = 10.0 V × (1 - 0.135335283)
Vc(2.00 s) = 10.0 V × 0.864664717
Vc(2.00 s) = 8.64664717 V ≈ 8.65 V

3. Resistor current at t = 2.00 s
The series current is:
i(t) = (V0/R)e^(-t/τ)

At t = 2.00 s:
i(2.00 s) = (10.0 V / 1.00×10^4 Ω) × 0.135335283
i(2.00 s) = (1.00×10^-3 A) × 0.135335283
i(2.00 s) = 1.35335283×10^-4 A
i(2.00 s) = 0.135335283 mA ≈ 0.135 mA

Because the requested positive direction is from the source toward the capacitor, this current is positive: +0.135 mA, i.e. +1.35×10^-4 A.

Consistency check:
The resistor voltage at t = 2.00 s is
VR = V0 - Vc = 10.0 V - 8.646647 V = 1.353353 V
Then
i = VR/R = 1.353353 V / 1.00×10^4 Ω = 1.353353×10^-4 A = 0.1353353 mA
This agrees with the exponential current expression. The initial current is V0/R = 1.00 mA; at t = 2.00 s = 2τ, it has decayed to 13.5% of that value, giving 0.135 mA.

Final answers:
- Time constant: τ = 1.00 s
- Capacitor voltage at t = 2.00 s: Vc = 8.65 V
- Resistor current at t = 2.00 s, positive from source toward capacitor: i = +0.135 mA = +1.35×10^-4 A

8.64664717 V = 8.64665 V within abs tolerance of key 8.64665 V
0.000135335283 A = 0.000135335 A within abs tolerance of key 0.000135335 A

question: Q15
answer:
Displacement-Channel Check — Extensometer on Unloaded Calibration Fixture

Scope and preconditions
- Extensometer is already mounted on the unloaded calibration fixture per the fixture instruction.
- Readout is in millimetres.
- Do not adjust the instrument between readings: do not re-zero, do not change gain/span, and do not reposition or mechanically adjust the extensometer. Only change the reference displacement as required by the sequence.
- Limits are inclusive: a value exactly equal to a limit is compliant.

Acceptance criteria
- For each nonzero reference displacement d = 1.000 mm and d = 2.000 mm: PASS if |R_d - d| <= 0.020 mm.
- For the final return-to-zero reading R_0 with reference 0.000 mm: PASS if |R_0 - 0.000| = |R_0| <= 0.010 mm.
- Overall verdict is PASS only if all three checks pass; otherwise FAIL.

Procedure
1. Zeroing step: With the fixture unloaded at zero displacement, zero the readout at zero displacement as required by the fixture instruction. Confirm the zeroed state. Do not re-zero later in the sequence.
2. Apply the 1.000 mm reference displacement. Record the reading R_1.000 = 1.010 mm. Compute the signed error E_1.000 = R_1.000 - 1.000 mm = 1.010 - 1.000 = +0.010 mm. Check |+0.010| <= 0.020 mm: PASS. Do not adjust the instrument.
3. Increase the reference displacement to 2.000 mm. Record the reading R_2.000 = 1.970 mm. Compute the signed error E_2.000 = R_2.000 - 2.000 mm = 1.970 - 2.000 = -0.030 mm. Check |-0.030| = 0.030 <= 0.020 mm: FAIL. Do not adjust the instrument.
4. Return the reference displacement to zero. Without re-zeroing or otherwise adjusting the instrument, record the final zero reading R_0 = 0.005 mm. Compute the signed error E_0 = R_0 - 0.000 mm = +0.005 mm. Check |+0.005| = 0.005 <= 0.010 mm: PASS.
5. Record the overall verdict. Any failed nonzero point makes the overall check FAIL. Here the 2.000 mm point fails, so the overall verdict is FAIL.

Check record

| Reference displacement (mm) | Reading (mm) | Signed error = reading - reference (mm) | Limit (mm) | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1.000 | 1.010 | +0.010 | ±0.020 | PASS |
| 2.000 | 1.970 | -0.030 | ±0.020 | FAIL |
| 0.000 (return, no re-zero) | 0.005 | +0.005 | |error| <= 0.010 | PASS |

Signed errors stated explicitly:
- At 1.000 mm reference: +0.010 mm
- At 2.000 mm reference: -0.030 mm
- At return to zero: +0.005 mm

Overall verdict: FAIL. The 1.000 mm and final-zero checks pass, but the 2.000 mm reading is out of tolerance by 0.010 mm beyond the allowed ±0.020 mm limit, since its error is -0.030 mm.

items.detail: zero at unloaded zero, apply and record 1.000 mm, apply and record 2.000 mm, then return to zero and record without re-zeroing
both inclusive limits (nonzero errors at most 0.020 mm, return zero at most 0.010 mm) are stated
0.01 mm = 1e-05 m within abs tolerance of key 1e-05 m; the 'pass' verdict is stated with the error
-0.03 mm = -3e-05 m within abs tolerance of key -3e-05 m; the 'fail' verdict is stated with the error
0.005 mm = 5e-06 m within abs tolerance of key 5e-06 m; the 'pass' verdict is stated with the error
the overall FAIL identifies the failed second reading as the cause

question: Q16
answer:
Use the linear thermal-expansion formula with the original length:

ΔL = α L0 ΔT

Given:
α = 12.0×10^-6 K^-1
L0 = 0.800 m
ΔT = 70.0 °C − 20.0 °C = 50.0 °C = 50.0 K

Compute the length increase:
ΔL = (12.0×10^-6 K^-1)(0.800 m)(50.0 K)
ΔL = 4.80×10^-4 m

Convert to millimetres:
ΔL = 4.80×10^-4 m × 1000 mm/m = 0.480 mm

Compute the final length using the original length plus the increase:
L = L0 + ΔL
L = 0.800 m + 0.000480 m
L = 0.80048 m

Answers:
1. The formula uses the original length L0 = 0.800 m: satisfied.
2. Length increase: 0.480 mm.
3. Final length: 0.80048 m.

Note: To three significant figures, consistent with the given inputs, the final length rounds to 0.800 m; the unrounded computed value is 0.80048 m.

question: Q17
answer:
# 29 CFR § 1910.147 — Minimum Tagout Attachment Strength and Periodic Inspection Interval

## 1. Direct answers

| Question | Answer | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum unlocking strength of tagout-device attachment means | **No less than 50 pounds** | § 1910.147(c)(5)(ii)(C)(2) |
| Frequency of employer's periodic inspection of the energy-control procedure | **At least annually** (i.e., no more than 12 months between inspections of each procedure) | § 1910.147(c)(6)(i) |

Both figures are floors, not targets: the strength is expressed as "no less than 50 pounds," and the inspection as "at least annually."

## 2. Governing text (verbatim)

**Strength — § 1910.147(c)(5)(ii)(C)(2)** (paragraph (C) is captioned *Substantial*; (C)(1) is the parallel lockout provision):

> "(2) Tagout devices, including and their means of attachment, shall be substantial enough to prevent inadvertent or accidental removal. Tagout device attachment means shall be of a non-reusable type, attachable by hand, self-locking, and non-releasable with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds and having the general design and basic characteristics of being at least equivalent to a one-piece, all-environment-tolerant nylon cable tie."

**Inspection — § 1910.147(c)(6)(i)** (paragraph (6) is captioned *Periodic inspection*):

> "(i) The employer shall conduct a periodic inspection of the energy control procedure at least annually to ensure that the procedure and the requirements of this standard are being followed.
> (A) The periodic inspection shall be perfomed by an authorized employee other than the ones(s) utilizing the energy control procedure being inspected.
> (B) The periodic inspection shall be conducted to correct any deviations or inadequacies identified.
> (C) Where lockout is used for energy control, the periodic inspection shall include a review, between the inspector and each authorized employee, of that employee's responsibilities under the energy control procedure being inspected.
> (D) Where tagout is used for energy control, the periodic inspection shall include a review, between the inspector and each authorized and affected employee, of that employee's responsibilities under the energy control procedure being inspected, and the elements set forth in paragraph (c)(7)(ii) of this section.
> (ii) The employer shall certify that the periodic inspections have been performed. The certification shall identify the machine or equipment on which the energy control procedure was being utilized, the date of the inspection, the employees included in the inspection, and the person performing the inspection."

(The typographical errors "perfomed" and "ones(s)" above are in the published text, not transcription errors on my part.)

## 3. Edition verification (Ask 1 — July 1, 2014 edition)

Status of the check, stated plainly: the text quoted in §2 was verified against the current eCFR rendering of § 1910.147 and against the U.S. Government Publishing Office print editions for **July 1, 2019** (CFR-2019-title29-vol5, § 1910.147, p. 502) and **July 1, 2025** (CFR-2025-title29-vol5, § 1910.147, p. 502). All three carry word-for-word identical language at (c)(5)(ii)(C)(2) and (c)(6)(i). The **July 1, 2014** print volume itself was not directly retrieved in this pass.

Why the values nonetheless stand for the 2014 edition: § 1910.147 was added by the final rule at 54 FR 36644 (Sept. 1, 1989), effective October 31, 1989, and the two provisions at issue have not been substantively amended since. Editions spanning 2014 to 2025 therefore contain the same operative text. For a documentary file, close the loop with one lookup: govinfo, `CFR-2014-title29-vol5`, § 1910.147, and confirm the strings "no less than 50 pounds" in (c)(5)(ii)(C)(2) and "at least annually" in (c)(6)(i). This is a verification step, not an open question — the answers do not change.

## 4. Safety-engineer application notes

**On the 50 pounds.** This is a performance requirement on the *attachment means* (the tie/strap), not on the tag itself, and not a prescribed test method. Read together, the clause requires the attachment means to be all four of: non-reusable (single-use — it is destroyed on removal, which is what makes removal evident), hand-attachable, self-locking, and non-releasable below 50 lbf. In procurement terms this means a one-piece, all-environment-tolerant nylon cable tie of at least 50-lb rated tensile/unlocking strength; the regulation's own benchmark is exactly that article. Do not specify 50 lb as a design target with no margin — specify "≥50 lb rated," and prefer ties with a published rating above 50 lb so that field variability (UV degradation, cold embrittlement, contamination of the locking pawl) does not erode the margin. A 50-lb pull test is *not* an OSHA-required acceptance test; if you perform one for QA, it is destructive and the sampled device must be discarded.

**On the annual inspection.** The obligation is per energy-control procedure, not one facility-wide event: each procedure in use must be inspected at least annually, by an authorized employee who is not one of the employees using that procedure. The output is not just a walk-through — it is a certification record under (c)(6)(ii) containing four data elements: the machine/equipment on which the procedure was used, the date, the employees included, and the person performing the inspection. Where tagout is used, the inspection must include a responsibilities review with each authorized **and** affected employee, plus the (c)(7)(ii) retraining elements. Practical control: calendar the annual date per procedure with a 30–60 day advance trigger, and treat a missed annual date as a compliance finding, not a scheduling slip.

**Tagout-only programs.** Non-mandatory Appendix A to § 1910.147 twice refers to "more rigorous periodic inspections" where tagout is used (both where the isolating device is not lockable and where tagout is applied to a lockable device with full employee protection under (c)(3)). Appendix A adds nothing enforceable to the standard, so the legal floor remains annual; but a defensible written program should set a shorter interval — quarterly is a common and prudent choice — for any procedure relying on tagout alone, and should say so explicitly in the procedure rather than defaulting to the annual minimum.

**Units.** "Pounds" in the regulation is pounds-force (lbf) in ordinary U.S. engineering usage — a force, not a mass. Do not convert to 22.2 kgf or 222 N in the compliance document; keep 50 pounds as written and add the metric equivalent only parenthetically if your program is bilingual.

## 5. Deliverable values

- Minimum unlocking strength of tagout-device attachment means: **50 pounds** (lbf), per § 1910.147(c)(5)(ii)(C)(2) — a floor, "no less than."
- Periodic inspection of the energy-control procedure: **at least annually**, per § 1910.147(c)(6)(i) — an interval ceiling of 12 months between inspections of each procedure, performed by an authorized employee other than the user(s), and certified per § 1910.147(c)(6)(ii).

items.detail: 50.0 pounds = 50 lb within rel tolerance of key 50 lb; the inclusive lower bound is stated
the at-least-annually inspection frequency is stated

question: Q18
answer:
Problem data and assumptions
- Simply supported prismatic beam, span L = 2.00 m.
- Central downward point load P = 1000 N at midspan.
- Rectangular cross-section: width b = 40.0 mm = 0.0400 m; vertical depth h = 60.0 mm = 0.0600 m.
- Young's modulus E = 200 GPa = 200 × 10^9 Pa.

- The 60.0 mm dimension is vertical, so bending occurs about the horizontal centroidal axis.

1. Maximum bending-moment magnitude
For a simply supported beam with a central point load, the maximum moment occurs at midspan and is
M_max = P L / 4
M_max = (1000 N)(2.00 m) / 4 = 500 N·m.
Magnitude: 500 N·m.

2. Second moment of area about the bending axis
For a solid rectangle bending about its horizontal centroidal axis,
I = b h^3 / 12
I = (0.0400 m)(0.0600 m)^3 / 12

answer:
## 1. Resistance selection and current

Using the ideal supply and the fixed LED forward drop:

\[
V_R = 9.00\,\mathrm{V} - 2.40\,\mathrm{V} = 6.60\,\mathrm{V}
\]

For each available resistance:

| \(R\) (\(\Omega\)) | \(I = V_R/R\) | Current in mA | Check against 18.0–22.0 mA inclusive | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 270 | \(6.60/270 = 0.024444\,\mathrm{A}\) | 24.44 mA | Above 22.0 mA | Reject |
| 330 | \(6.60/330 = 0.020000\,\mathrm{A}\) | 20.00 mA | Inside window | Select |
| 390 | \(6.60/390 = 0.016923\,\mathrm{A}\) | 16.92 mA | Below 18.0 mA | Reject |

The 330 \(\Omega\) resistor gives exactly 20.0 mA, which is within the required 18.0–22.0 mA inclusive range. Therefore the selected series resistor is **330 \(\Omega\)**.

## 2. Checks of the other resistance choices

- **270 \(\Omega\):** \(I = 6.60/270 = 24.44\,\mathrm{mA}\). This exceeds the upper limit of 22.0 mA, so it is rejected.
- **330 \(\Omega\):** \(I = 6.60/330 = 20.00\,\mathrm{mA}\). This is within 18.0–22.0 mA inclusive, so it is accepted.
- **390 \(\Omega\):** \(I = 6.60/390 = 16.92\,\mathrm{mA}\). This is below the lower limit of 18.0 mA, so it is rejected.

Only the 330 \(\Omega\) choice passes the current requirement. No series or parallel combinations are used; the resistance values are treated as exact nominal values with negligible tolerance.

## 3. Dissipation and power-rating selection

For the selected 330 \(\Omega\) resistor carrying 20.00 mA:

\[
P_R = I^2R = (0.02000\,\mathrm{A})^2(330\,\Omega) = 0.132\,\mathrm{W}
\]

Equivalently:

\[
P_R = \frac{V_R^2}{R} = \frac{(6.60\,\mathrm{V})^2}{330\,\Omega} = \frac{43.56}{330} = 0.132\,\mathrm{W}
\]

The required power rating is at least twice the actual dissipation, with equality allowed:

\[
P_{\mathrm{rating}} \ge 2P_R = 2(0.132\,\mathrm{W}) = 0.264\,\mathrm{W}
\]

Check the available ratings:

| Rating | Compare to 0.264 W | Result |
|---:|---|---|
| 0.125 W | \(0.125 < 0.264\) | Fail |
| 0.250 W | \(0.250 < 0.264\) | Fail |
| 0.500 W | \(0.500 \ge 0.264\) | Pass |

The smallest available rating that satisfies the \(2\times\) derating requirement is **0.500 W**.

Final specified resistor: **330 \(\Omega\), 0.500 W**.

question: Q20
answer:
# Collection Check FC-CV-01 — Water Flowmeter on an Assembled Atmospheric-Discharge Bench

**Revision:** 1  |  **Bench state:** already assembled — verification only, no assembly steps  |  **Acceptance limit:** |signed indication error| <= 3.0 %

## 1. Scope

Single-setpoint volumetric (timed-collection) verification of the bench water flowmeter at an indicated 12.0 L/min on an assembled bench whose discharge is to atmosphere (open vessel, no downstream throttling, meter sees essentially zero backpressure). One run constitutes one check record.

## 2. Definitions and acceptance

| Symbol | Definition | Value in this run |
|---|---|---|
| Q_ind | Meter indicated flow, held at setpoint | 12.0 L/min |
| V_coll | Volume read from the collection vessel after the timed interval | 11.76 L |
| t_coll | Collection interval | 60.0 s |
| Q_ref | Reference flow: Q_ref = V_coll x (60 s/min) / t_coll | computed below |
| E | Signed indication error: E = 100 x (Q_ind - Q_ref) / Q_ref | computed below |

- Sign convention: **E > 0 means the meter over-indicates** (reads high) relative to the collected reference; E < 0 means it under-indicates.
- E is a percentage **of the reference flow (i.e. of reading)**, exactly as the given definition states — not a percentage of full scale/span.
- **Pass criterion: |E| <= 3.0 %.** The criterion is applied to the error alone; measurement uncertainty is not added to the error (see Section 8).

## 3. Equipment and prerequisites

| Item | Requirement | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Flowmeter under test | Bench-mounted; indication resolution <= 0.1 L/min | Resolution must be small against the 3.0 % margin (0.1/12.0 = 0.8 %) |
| Three-way diverter | Upstream of discharge, switches full bore between return tank and collection vessel with no trapped dead volume | Diversion is the timing trigger; both transitions must be quick and symmetric |
| Collection vessel | Volumetric, graduations readable to <= 0.05 L, capacity >= 15 L, open top, level and clean | Upper pass bound is 12.37 L; 15 L leaves freeboard |
| Timer | Resolution <= 0.1 s, start/stop actuated at the diverter | Timing is the dominant uncertainty term |
| Return tank | Open to atmosphere | Keeps the pump operating point stable during the setpoint hold |
| Water | Bench supply, no visible air entrainment | Entrained air biases the collected volume low |
| Discharge outlet height | Outlet stays clear of the vessel water line for the whole collection; allow >= 200 mm freeboard on a 300 mm-diameter vessel (11.76 L raises the level ~166 mm) | If the outlet submerges, backpressure rises mid-run and both meter reading and reference flow shift |

No temperature or density correction is applied: the meter and the collection vessel measure the same water at the same bench temperature, so the comparison is volumetric-to-volumetric. Record water temperature for the record only.

## 4. Procedure

| # | Action | Record / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pre-check the assembled bench: no leaks, discharge open to atmosphere, diverter free to move, vessel empty/dry/level, timer zeroed. Record water temperature. | Bench verified; temperature recorded |
| 2 | Set the diverter so flow goes to the **return tank**. | Flow bypasses the vessel |
| 3 | **Start the pump** with flow already diverted to the return tank. | Pump running, all flow to return |
| 4 | **Adjust the flow-control valve until the meter indicates 12.0 L/min.** | Q_ind = 12.0 L/min |
| 5 | **Hold that indication steady for 30 s.** | Indication must stay within 11.9–12.1 L/min (+/-0.1 L/min) for the whole hold; record start and end values |
| 6 | **Zero the collection-volume reading** with the vessel empty and in its collection position. | Reading = 0.00 L |
| 7 | **Start the timer and, in the same motion, divert flow into the collection vessel.** The diverter is the trigger for both. | t = 0.0 s, collection begins |
| 8 | **Collect for 60.0 s. Do not adjust flow** — do not touch the flow-control valve, the pump speed, or any other flow-setting element during collection. | Record indication at t = 30 s; must still read 12.0 +/- 0.1 L/min |
| 9 | At t = 60.0 s, **simultaneously divert flow back to the return tank and stop the timer.** | t_coll = 60.0 s, flow back on return |
| 10 | **Read the collected volume** from the vessel while the pump is still running and the discharge is still at its operating condition. | V_coll = 11.76 L |
| 11 | **Only now stop the pump.** | Pump stopped |
| 12 | Compute Q_ref and E; enter the verdict. | Section 6 |

Sequencing rationale: the pump is started only after flow is on the return tank, so the setpoint is established before any water enters the vessel; the volume is read **before** the pump is stopped, so the reading is taken with the discharge line still at its running condition and no drain-back or siphon can alter the vessel contents between the end of timing and the reading.

## 5. Data record

| Item | Symbol | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indicated flow at setpoint | Q_ind | 12.0 | L/min |
| Setpoint hold duration | — | 30 | s |
| Indication at end of hold / at t = 30 s of collection | — | 12.0 | L/min |
| Collection interval | t_coll | 60.0 | s |
| Zeroed collection reading | — | 0.00 | L |
| Collected volume | V_coll | 11.76 | L |
| Water temperature | theta | recorded | degC |

## 6. Calculation

Reference flow (collected volume over measured time):

    Q_ref = V_coll x 60 / t_coll = 11.76 L x 60 s/min / 60.0 s = 11.76 L/min

Signed indication error:

    E = 100 x (Q_ind - Q_ref) / Q_ref
      = 100 x (12.0 - 11.76) / 11.76
      = 100 x 0.24 / 11.76
      = +2.0408 %
      -> E = +2.04 %  (meter over-indicates by 0.24 L/min)

## 7. Verdict

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Reference flow Q_ref | **11.76 L/min** |
| Signed indication error E | **+2.04 %** (over-indicating) |
| |E| vs limit | 2.04 % vs 3.0 % |
| Margin to limit | 0.96 percentage points |
| **Verdict** | **PASS** |

The meter's indication error magnitude is 2.04 %, which is less than or equal to the 3.0 % acceptance limit. The unit passes this collection check at the 12.0 L/min setpoint.

## 8. Pass windows and measurement-uncertainty note

Derived pass windows for re-use at the same setpoint and interval (Q_ind = 12.0 L/min, t_coll = 60.0 s):

- Collected volume must lie in **11.65 L to 12.37 L** (from 12.0/1.03 and 12.0/0.97). Measured 11.76 L sits 0.11 L above the lower bound.
- Equivalently, at Q_ref = 11.76 L/min the meter indication must lie in **11.41 L/min to 12.11 L/min**.
- Timing break-even is t_coll = 60.56 s (+0.56 s); volume break-even is 11.65 L (-0.11 L).
- Worst case within stated tolerances (volume read +/-0.05 L, timing +/-0.2 s: V = 11.71 L, t = 60.2 s) gives Q_ref = 11.67 L/min and E = +2.82 %, still inside 3.0 %. The PASS is therefore robust to the stated instrument and operator tolerances, not just to the nominal numbers.

If |E| exceeds 3.0 %, repeat the run once from step 1; if the repeat confirms the deviation, the meter fails this check and requires calibration/adjustment before the bench is returned to service.

## 9. Record block

Check ID: FC-CV-01  |  Setpoint: 12.0 L/min  |  Interval: 60.0 s  |  V_coll: 11.76 L  |  Q_ref: 11.76 L/min  |  E: +2.04 %  |  Limit: |E| <= 3.0 %  |  Verdict: PASS  |  Operator: ________  |  Date: ________  |  Water temp: ______ degC  |  Instrument IDs: ________

zero before divert before collect: True; diversion and timer together: True; 60.0 s stated: True; no adjustment stated: False - all are required
diversion back and timer stop happen together, the volume is read, and only then is the pump stopped
11.76 L/min = 11.76 L/min within abs tolerance of key 11.76 L/min
the signed error 2.0408% carries its positive sign (or an over-reading statement)
the inclusive 3.0% magnitude limit and the passing verdict are stated

question: Q21
answer:
Adiabatic mixing calculation for water in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity.

Given:
- m_hot = 1.00 kg at T_hot = 80.0 °C
- m_cold = 3.00 kg at T_cold = 20.0 °C
- c_p = 4200 J/(kg·K), constant for both portions
- No heat loss to the vessel or surroundings; no phase change

Energy balance:
Heat lost by the hot water equals heat gained by the cold water:
Q_hot_out = Q_cold_in
m_hot c_p (T_hot - T_f) = m_cold c_p (T_f - T_cold)

Because c_p is the same constant for both portions, it cancels:
m_hot (T_hot - T_f) = m_cold (T_f - T_cold)

Solve for T_f:
m_hot T_hot - m_hot T_f = m_cold T_f - m_cold T_cold
m_hot T_hot + m_cold T_cold = (m_hot + m_cold) T_f
T_f = (m_hot T_hot + m_cold T_cold) / (m_hot + m_cold)

Substitute values:
T_f = [(1.00 kg)(80.0 °C) + (3.00 kg)(20.0 °C)] / (1.00 kg + 3.00 kg)
T_f = (80.0 + 60.0) / 4.00 °C
T_f = 140.0 / 4.00 °C
T_f = 35.0 °C

Check using heat quantities with c_p = 4200 J/(kg·K):
Q_hot_out = (1.00)(4200)(80.0 - 35.0) = 189000 J
Q_cold_in = (3.00)(4200)(35.0 - 20.0) = 189000 J
These are equal, confirming the energy balance.

Final uniform temperature:
T_f = 35.0 °C = 308.15 K

Significant figures: the inputs are given to 3 significant figures, so the final temperature is reported as 35.0 °C. The result lies between 20.0 °C and 80.0 °C and is closer to the initial cold-water temperature, as expected from the 3:1 cold-to-hot mass ratio.

items.detail: 35.0 deg C = 35 deg C within abs tolerance of key 35 deg C

question: Q22
answer:
Safety Engineer determination under 29 CFR § 1910.95(g), July 1, 2014 edition.

| Ask | Requirement | Answer | Governing provision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deadline to establish a baseline audiogram after first exposure at or above the action level, where the mobile-test-van exception is not used | Within 6 months of first exposure | § 1910.95(g)(5)(i) |
| 2 | Minimum workplace-noise-free period preceding a baseline audiogram when hearing protectors are not used as a substitute | At least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise | § 1910.95(g)(5)(iii) |
| 3 | Allowed retest window after an annual audiogram shows a standard threshold shift | Within 30 days | § 1910.95(g)(7)(ii) |

Regulatory basis:

1. § 1910.95(g)(5)(i) — Baseline audiogram. "Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram against which subsequent audiograms can be compared." The 1-year period in § 1910.95(g)(5)(ii) applies only where mobile test vans are used to meet the audiometric testing obligation; because the question excludes that exception, the 6-month deadline controls.

2. § 1910.95(g)(5)(iii) — "Testing to establish a baseline audiogram shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise. Hearing protectors may be used as a substitute for the requirement that baseline audiograms be preceded by 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise." Because hearing protectors are not used as a substitute in the question, the full minimum 14-hour workplace-noise-free period applies. The employer must also notify employees of the need to avoid high levels of non-occupational noise during the 14-hour period immediately preceding the examination, per § 1910.95(g)(5)(iv).

3. § 1910.95(g)(7)(ii) — "If the annual audiogram shows that an employee has suffered a standard threshold shift, the employer may obtain a retest within 30 days and consider the results of the retest as the annual audiogram." The retest is permissive, but if the employer uses a retest in place of the annual audiogram, it must be obtained within 30 days. This is distinct from the 21-day written notification requirement in § 1910.95(g)(8), which is not the retest window.

Notes and boundaries:
- The action level for purposes of § 1910.95(g) is an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 dBA.
- A standard threshold shift is defined in § 1910.95(g)(10)(i) as an average change of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear relative to the baseline audiogram.
- The answer addresses only the three requested values. No plan falsifiers, kill triggers, or assumption tables are included because the request does not ask for them.

question: Q23
answer:
PROBLEM: Two bars, side by side between rigid end plates, same initial length L = 1.00 m = 1000 mm, initially stress-free, no temperature change, linear elastic. Aluminum: A_al = 200 mm^2, E_al = 70.0 GPa. Steel: A_st = 100 mm^2, E_st = 200 mm^2... E_st = 200 GPa. Total axial tensile load P = 30.0 kN applied through the rigid plates. Find common extension, stress in each bar, force in each bar.

1) COMPATIBILITY (rigid, parallel end plates)
The plates stay parallel and both bars are bonded to them, so both bars undergo the same axial extension delta and the same strain:
  delta_al = delta_st = delta ;  eps = delta / L (same for both).

2) CONSTITUTIVE LAW (linear, isothermal)
  sigma_i = E_i * eps ;  P_i = sigma_i * A_i = E_i * A_i * eps = (E_i A_i / L) * delta.
Each bar behaves as an axial spring of stiffness k_i = E_i A_i / L.

3) AXIAL STIFFNESSES (consistent units: N and mm)
  E_al = 70.0 GPa = 70,000 N/mm^2 ;  E_st = 200 GPa = 200,000 N/mm^2
  k_al = E_al*A_al/L = 70,000 * 200 / 1000 = 14,000 N/mm
  k_st = E_st*A_st/L = 200,000 * 100 / 1000 = 20,000 N/mm
  Sum k = 34,000 N/mm
(Equivalently EA_al = 14.0e6 N = 14,000 kN, EA_st = 20.0e6 N = 20,000 kN, sum = 34.0e6 N.)

4) EQUILIBRIUM
The plate transmits the full load to the two bars in parallel:
  P_al + P_st = P = 30.0 kN = 30,000 N.

5) COMMON EXTENSION
  delta = P / (k_al + k_st) = 30,000 N / 34,000 N/mm = 0.88235 mm
  delta = 0.882 mm  (strain eps = 0.88235/1000 = 8.82e-4)

6) FORCE IN EACH BAR
  P_i = P * (E_i A_i) / (E_al A_al + E_st A_st)   [same L for both, so L cancels]
  P_al = 30.0 kN * 14.0/34.0 = 12.3529 kN -> 12.4 kN  (12,353 N)
  P_st = 30.0 kN * 20.0/34.0 = 17.6471 kN -> 17.6 kN  (17,647 N)
  Check: 12.353 + 17.647 = 30.000 kN = applied load. OK.
  Note: 12.4 + 17.6 = 30.0 kN after rounding as well.

7) TENSILE STRESS IN EACH BAR
  sigma_al = P_al / A_al = 12,352.9 N / 200 mm^2 = 61.76 MPa -> 61.8 MPa
  sigma_st = P_st / A_st = 17,647.1 N / 100 mm^2 = 176.47 MPa -> 176 MPa

8) VERIFICATION
(a) Compatibility: delta from aluminum = P_al L/(E_al A_al) = 12,352.9*1000/14.0e6 = 0.88235 mm; delta from steel = 17,647.1*1000/20.0e6 = 0.88235 mm. Identical — requirement met.
(b) Equilibrium: forces sum to 30.0 kN.
(c) Strain consistency: eps_al = 61.76/70,000 = 8.823e-4; eps_st = 176.47/200,000 = 8.823e-4. Equal strains, as required by the rigid plates.
(d) Linear-elastic validity: 61.8 MPa is far below any common aluminum alloy yield (~100-500 MPa) and 176 MPa is below typical structural-steel yield (~250 MPa), so the linear-elastic, no-yield assumption is consistent with the computed stresses. No computed value exceeds a limit stated in this solution.
(e) Stiffer-but-smaller steel bar takes 58.8% of the load (EA fraction 20/34); aluminum takes 41.2% (14/34). Because steel's area is half of aluminum's, its stress is ~2.86x larger despite carrying only ~1.43x the force — the expected qualitative result.

9) ANSWERS (3 significant figures, consistent with the 3-s.f. input data)
  Common extension: delta = 0.882 mm (0.88235 mm unrounded; strain 8.82e-4)
  Tensile stress: aluminum 61.8 MPa; steel 176 MPa
  Force carried: aluminum 12.4 kN; steel 17.6 kN
  (Rounded values reproduce the 30.0 kN total exactly; unrounded values sum to 30.000 kN.)

ASSUMPTIONS (implied by the statement, listed for completeness): plates are rigid and remain parallel; perfect bond, no slip; purely axial loading with no eccentricity or bending; uniform sections and moduli; end effects, self-weight and stress concentrations neglected; small strains, linear elasticity, isothermal.

question: Q24
answer:
## 1. Pulley selection and diameter ratio

For an ideal open-belt drive, the driven speed is

\[
n_2 = n_1 \frac{D_1}{D_2}
\]

with \(D_1 = 80.0\,\mathrm{mm}\) and \(n_1 = 1500\,\mathrm{rpm}\). The minimum driven diameter that can satisfy \(n_2 \le 500\,\mathrm{rpm}\) is

\[
D_2 \ge D_1 \frac{n_1}{n_{2,\max}}
= 80.0\,\mathrm{mm} \times \frac{1500}{500}
= 240\,\mathrm{mm}.
\]

Candidate check:

| Driven pitch diameter \(D_2\) (mm) | Output speed \(n_2 = 1500 \times 80/D_2\) (rpm) | Meets \(n_2 \le 500\,\mathrm{rpm}\)? |
|---:|---:|:---:|
| 160 | 750 | No |
| 200 | 600 | No |
| 240 | 500 | Yes, equality allowed |

Smallest qualifying driven pulley: **\(D_2 = 240\,\mathrm{mm}\)**.

Diameter ratio:

\[
\frac{D_2}{D_1} = \frac{240}{80.0} = 3.00
\]

So the driven/driver diameter ratio is **3.00**, equivalently \(D_1:D_2 = 1:3\). The speed ratio is \(n_1:n_2 = 3:1\).

## 2. Output speed, rotation direction, and torque

Output speed:

\[
n_2 = 1500\,\mathrm{rpm} \times \frac{80.0}{240}
= 500\,\mathrm{rpm}
\]

Thus the output speed is **500 rpm**, which satisfies the requirement \(n_2 \le 500\,\mathrm{rpm}\); equality is permitted.

Rotation direction: for an **open-belt drive**, the two shafts rotate in the **same direction** when viewed from the same side of both shafts. If the driver is clockwise viewed from that side, the driven pulley is also clockwise.

Output torque under the ideal no-slip, no-power-loss assumption:

\[
T_2 = T_1 \frac{D_2}{D_1}
= 4.00\,\mathrm{N\,m} \times \frac{240}{80.0}
= 12.0\,\mathrm{N\,m}
\]

Power check:

\[
P_{\mathrm{in}} = T_1 \omega_1
= 4.00 \times \left(1500 \times \frac{2\pi}{60}\right)
= 628.3\,\mathrm{W}
\]

\[
P_{\mathrm{out}} = T_2 \omega_2
= 12.0 \times \left(500 \times \frac{2\pi}{60}\right)
= 628.3\,\mathrm{W}
\]

So the ideal drive conserves power.

## 3. Belt linear speed

The belt linear speed at the pitch line is

\[
v = \pi D_1 n_1
= \pi (0.0800\,\mathrm{m})\left(\frac{1500}{60}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\right)
= 2\pi\,\mathrm{m/s}
\approx 6.283\,\mathrm{m/s}
\]

Check at the driven pulley:

\[
v = \pi D_2 n_2
= \pi (0.240\,\mathrm{m})\left(\frac{500}{60}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\right)
= 2\pi\,\mathrm{m/s}
